nf2_design_input.NF2: trusted raw-path library context lacks principal enforcement
NF2_CURRENT_MECHANICS: principal enters OperationContext through ingress.execute(principal=...) as a plain str; defaults: 'library' (ingress default), 'cli' (CLI), 'hermes' (adapter constant PRINCIPAL in adapters/hermes/invoke.py); no derivation, no verification
ContextResolver.resolve() stores principal verbatim; OperationContext.principal is identity-only metadata; the ingress audit record (_audit) does NOT include principal

trusted resource roots enter via adapters/host/resources.py host_resource_config_from_env() from the AOTA_FORGE_HOST_ROOT_* env allowlist, or an explicitly constructed TrustedResourceConfig; the model can never configure roots

trusted adapter paths (registry_path/pidfile/receipt) and logical refs (*_id) enter through TRUSTED_ADAPTER_KEYS into ctx.params/ctx.trusted; handlers resolve them to raw paths and open files (handlers.py _handle_host_status: Path(registry_path), host_process_status(Path(pidfile)), read_receipt(Path(receipt)))
raw resolved paths exist after logical resolution inside handlers (TrustedResourceResolver.resolve returns a Path; adapters/host/resources.py resolve_host_resource returns {kind, resource_id, path})
no current enforcement couples principal to authority: only mechanical gates exist (read-only gate, contract validation, trusted-channel bounds)
nf2_design_input.NF2_AUTHORITY_GAP: principal is a free-form self-asserted string with zero enforcement: any library caller can pass any principal while also supplying trusted resolved paths through the trusted channel; no principal-to-trusted-root coupling, no principal-to-operation coupling, no principal-to-audit coupling; adapters can effectively self-assert principal (hermes PRINCIPAL constant). 'Who may use the trusted raw-path library context' is not enforced at all.
NF2_M3_A2_INPUT: decide whether principal becomes a typed executor-neutral identity (e.g. principal-of-record) vs trusted adapter metadata (OQ-M3A2-02)
decide whether the trusted adapter channel / raw resolved paths require principal-bound authority or capability lease (OQ-M3A2-03)
decide whether the canonical audit record must include principal
decide how adapter self-assertion is constrained (derived from adapter identity rather than free-form string)

i9_b008_design_input.I9_B008: canonical ingress may allow malformed non-dict handler payload to escape canonical error envelope
i9_b008_design_input.I9_B008_CURRENT_SEAM: aota_forge/core/ingress.py execute(): the handler invocation `payload = handler(context)` is guarded by try/except (ForgeError + bounded generic guard), but the success normalization block after `if isinstance(payload, dict) and payload.get('ok') is False:` calls payload.get(...) unconditionally on the assumption payload is a dict; a non-dict handler return (list/str/None/int) raises AttributeError OUTSIDE any guard and escapes execute(), violating the documented invariant 'Never raises ForgeError; canonical errors are returned in the envelope'. Exact seam: from `audit['handler'] = 'success'` through the `return success(...)` block (ingress.py, handler-success normalization).
i9_b008_design_input.I9_B008_DESIGN_IMPACT: envelope-totality invariant; orthogonal to the durable subject graph schema and the authority model; affects the canonical result contract robustness and audit integrity; must hold before any M3-B write handler exists so a malformed mutation handler payload cannot escape the envelope.
i9_b008_design_input.not_fixed: M3-A0 records the seam only; no repair performed (see guard static check on ingress.py marker).
